bug_semantics: An authenticated backend user with backend.manage_editor could save attacker-controlled LESS in Editor Settings -> Markup Styles. EditorSetting::compileCss() concatenated html_custom_styles into a .fr-view rule and returned Less_Parser output; LESS escaped-string syntax such as ~"</style><script>alert(1)</script><style>" preserved HTML delimiters. After the output-side strip_tags() call was removed, _custom_styles.php embedded that compiled string verbatim inside a <style> element used by the normal and authentication backend layouts, allowing stored CSS to terminate the style element and execute script when another backend user loaded a page.
flaw_origin: Commit c9dab67bc819b791df8432a898dd976f19388a87 changed only the exception path to e($ex->getMessage()) in EditorSetting::renderCss(), but simultaneously replaced <?= strip_tags(EditorSetting::renderCss()) ?> with the raw <?= EditorSetting::renderCss() ?> sink in modules/backend/layouts/_custom_styles.php. Escaping exception text did not sanitize successfully compiled, attacker-controlled LESS output, so this commit removed the defense from the successful compilation path without replacing it.
ai_marker: absent: git cat-file -p c9dab67bc819b791df8432a898dd976f19388a87 shows author Luke Towers <git@luketowers.ca> and committer Luke Towers <git@luketowers.ca>; its commit message has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI trailer/marker.
evidence: The first-party advisory https://github.com/wintercms/winter/security/advisories/GHSA-vgp4-2fc4-qff2 identifies winter/wn-backend-module 1.2.10, 1.2.11, and 1.2.12 as affected, 1.2.13 as patched, backend.manage_editor as the required permission, LESS compilation followed by rendering on every backend page as the path, and d28f0b9474af79cfaa80eeb9d691f7a7c4469720 as the patch. At c9dab67bc819b791df8432a898dd976f19388a87, git grep shows modules/backend/models/editorsetting/fields.yaml:8 exposes html_custom_styles, modules/backend/ServiceProvider.php:289 assigns that settings model to backend.manage_editor, EditorSetting.php:264-272 parses self::get('html_custom_styles') with Less_Parser and returns getCss(), _custom_styles.php:12 prints EditorSetting::renderCss() raw inside <style>, and layouts/_head.php:85 plus layouts/auth.php:64 include that partial. The d28f0b9 fix tests use .x { content: ~"</style><script>alert(1)</script><style>"; }, directly demonstrating the style-breakout mechanism. git log -L 10,12:modules/backend/layouts/_custom_styles.php traces the relevant sink: ef290df3af545b2e0ca28fc1773dc0399b555f72 originally added raw rendering in 2016, a9a2c6e83b2d2455c62640075f5833ae953b7b02 added strip_tags() in 2020, and c9dab67bc819b791df8432a898dd976f19388a87 removed it on 2026-01-14. Direct parent-tree verification with git grep at 22df8f1d6d8e95487e385bd4f052d0c772a2b3fc finds _custom_styles.php:12 as <?= strip_tags(EditorSetting::renderCss()) ?>, while the BIC tree has <?= EditorSetting::renderCss() ?>, so the vulnerable condition is absent in the immediate parent. git cat-file -p shows c9dab67b has the single parent 22df8f1d6d8e95487e385bd4f052d0c772a2b3fc, making it the direct atomic change rather than a merge/release aggregate. git tag --contains c9dab67b starts at v1.2.10 and lists v1.2.10-v1.2.14, not v1.2.9; v1.2.9 tree still has the sink-level strip_tags(). v1.2.12's EditorSetting.php:259 still returns $customCss, whereas v1.2.13's line 260 returns strip_tags($customCss). git tag --contains d28f0b9474af79cfaa80eeb9d691f7a7c4469720 lists v1.2.13 and v1.2.14 only. The fix diff moves the protection into both renderCss() methods by changing return $customCss to return strip_tags($customCss), including the cached/successful output consumed by the layouts.
reasoning: The vulnerable feature itself predates the affected range, but it was not exploitable through this editor-style sink immediately before the BIC because a9a2c6e83b2d2455c62640075f5833ae953b7b02 had wrapped the rendered editor CSS with strip_tags(). Line history isolates c9dab67bc819b791df8432a898dd976f19388a87 as the smallest commit that removed that guard; selecting the later v1.2.10 merge would be selecting a release aggregate, and selecting the 2016 feature commit would ignore the intervening defense and fail immediate-parent absence. The BIC parent directly contains the sanitizer, the BIC directly replaces it with a raw sink, and tag ancestry aligns that transition exactly with the advisory's 1.2.10 lower boundary. The successful LESS path accepts stored administrative input, returns compiled output capable of containing a closing style tag, caches it, and the backend layouts render it on subsequent pages. d28f0b9474af79cfaa80eeb9d691f7a7c4469720 restores sanitization at renderCss() before the v1.2.13 boundary, including the same payload in regression tests. Finally, the BIC commit object has a human author/committer and no AI attribution marker or trailer. Under the BIC-only attribution rule, the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
